title: Halle Berry Accused of Choking 12-Year-Old Son as Ex Seeks Sole Custody in Restraining Order
body:
Hollywood veteran Halle Berry is once again at the center of a family‑law dispute after her former husband, French actor Olivier Martinez, filed a temporary restraining order alleging that the Oscar‑winning star physically assaulted their 12‑year‑old son, Maceo. In a filing submitted to a Los Angeles family‑court judge, Martinez claims Berry “choked” the boy during a heated argument on September 26, and he is now seeking sole physical custody of the child. The allegations have ignited a fresh wave of media scrutiny, adding to the actress’s long‑standing legal battles and raising questions about the impact of high‑profile divorces on children.

The restraining order request, which was made public through court documents, details an incident in which Martinez says Berry “jumped on” Maceo and placed her hands around his throat, causing the child to gasp for air. According to the petition, the alleged assault was witnessed by a family friend who subsequently called the police, prompting a brief investigation that was later closed without charges. Martinez’s attorneys argue that the episode is part of a pattern of “intimidating and violent behavior” by Berry, and they are asking the court to grant him exclusive physical custody while Berry is barred from contacting the child except through supervised visitation.

Berry’s legal team has responded swiftly, denying the accusations and labeling the filing as “baseless and intended to manipulate custody proceedings.” In a brief statement, the actress’ representatives emphasized that Berry has always prioritized her son’s well‑being and that the allegations are “unfounded and designed to distract from Martinez’s own conduct.” They also noted that Berry has previously been the subject of false claims in past disputes, referencing a 2021 lawsuit in which she was accused of violating a non‑disclosure agreement—claims that were ultimately dismissed.

The case arrives amid a broader pattern of contentious custody battles involving celebrities, where public perception often collides with private family dynamics. Legal experts point out that temporary restraining orders in family‑court contexts are not uncommon; they serve as a protective measure while a more thorough hearing determines the merits of the allegations. However, they also caution that such filings can have lasting repercussions on both parental rights and the child’s emotional health, especially when the dispute is aired in the public eye. “When a high‑profile parent is accused of violence, the court must balance the safety of the child with the presumption of innocence for the accused,” said family‑law attorney Maya Patel, who has handled several celebrity cases.

Industry observers note that Berry’s career, already under the shadow of recent legal entanglements—including a defamation lawsuit involving a former business partner—could suffer further setbacks if the allegations gain traction. The actress has been relatively quiet on the matter, focusing on her upcoming film projects and philanthropic work, but the intensity of the media coverage suggests that her public image may be tested again. Meanwhile, Martinez, who has largely stayed out of the limelight since his 2012 marriage to Berry ended, appears to be leveraging the legal system to secure a more favorable custody arrangement, a move that could be interpreted as either a genuine concern for his son’s safety or a strategic bid for leverage.

As the case moves toward a full hearing, a judge will likely order a comprehensive evaluation, including psychological assessments of both parents and the child, as well as testimonies from witnesses and possibly a child‑protective services review. The outcome will hinge on the credibility of the evidence presented and the ability of each party to demonstrate a stable, nurturing environment for Maceo. Regardless of the verdict, the situation underscores the challenges of navigating parental responsibilities under the glare of fame, and it may prompt a broader conversation about how courts handle domestic‑violence allegations involving public figures.

In the weeks ahead, both Berry and Martinez will be under intense scrutiny as the legal process unfolds. While the restraining order remains temporary, its existence signals a potentially protracted custody battle that could reshape the family’s dynamic for years to come. Observers will be watching closely to see whether the court’s decision prioritizes the child’s safety and stability above the sensational headlines that inevitably accompany Hollywood disputes.
